study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate the degree to which case-control analyses disguise interindividual differences in brain structure among patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and to map the brain alterations linked to these disorders at the level of individual patients.

rci9_quality_checking_detail.answer: The quality of all MRI scans was checked using the 'weighted overall image quality' metric provided by the CAT12 toolbox. All participants included in our cohort scored < 2.8, where lower scores denote higher image quality. On the rating scale provided by the authors of this tool, this corresponds to a rating of 'good' for 99.1% of our scans and a small number (0.9%) as 'satisfactory'.
rci9_quality_checking_detail.reason: The details of the quality checking are provided in the supplementary material.
rci9_quality_checking_detail.supporting_text: Regarding image quality, we carefully checked the quality of all MRI scans included in our model using the 'weighted overall image quality' metric provided by the CAT12 toolbox. Whilst this does not assess the effect of head motion directly, it provides a reasonable estimate of overall image quality which is influenced by head motion. On this metric, all participants included in our cohort scored < 2.8, where lower scores denote higher image quality. On the rating scale provided by the authors of this tool (see www.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat/index.html#QA), this corresponds to a rating of 'good' for 99.1% of our scans and a small number (0.9%) as 'satisfactory'.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: We tested for associations between the percentage of extremely deviating voxels and age, disease duration, and cognitive performance. We corrected for the number of regressions (n = 12) within each disorder and modality using the Bonferroni-Holm method. A corrected threshold P < .05 was considered to be statistically significant.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Individual deviations from the normative model were frequent but highly heterogeneous in both schizophrenia and bipolar disorder; overlap >2% occurred only in few loci, with schizophrenia showing mean gray matter reductions in frontal, temporal, and cerebellar regions and bipolar disorder primarily in cerebellum.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using GPR-based normative models, patients exhibited significantly more extreme deviations than controls, yet voxelwise overlap across patients exceeded 2% only in limited regions. Schizophrenia showed mean negative deviations in frontal, temporal, and cerebellar gray matter, while bipolar disorder showed mean deviations predominantly in cerebellar regions. Associations indicated that, in schizophrenia, extreme positive white matter deviations related to longer disease duration, and in bipolar disorder, greater extreme negative gray matter deviations related to lower processing speed and executive function (eTable 2). Conclusions replicated under FDR-based thresholding of extremes (supplement).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Demonstrates normative modeling for individual-level mapping; suggests moving beyond case–control averages; proposes future stratification via clustering of deviation patterns and multimodal integration; supplementary FreeSurfer analyses support VBM findings.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; specific confound handling (e.g., medication, substance abuse, motion) is exploratory and limited; only general image quality metric used; single-site acquisition may limit generalizability.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study used a 1.5T Siemens MAGNETOM Sonata scanner. The primary analysis was at the voxel level (VBM) with an 8mm FWHM smoothing kernel. A secondary analysis was performed using Freesurfer v5.3 to extract cortical thickness and surface area with a 10mm FWHM smoothing kernel. All analyses were performed in Python 3.6. PALM was used for permutation-based inference.
